messages:
incident-bot: ALERT -> KV-cache continuous-batching error rate and p95 latency spike for redwood-hosted models. Alert: kv_cache_evictions_up  ->  runbook: https://go/internal/runbooks/kv-cache-batch-regressions. Paging oncall.

maria: ack. I'm on the page, grabbing dashboards (console -> /dashboards/kv-cache). Seeing eviction count + CPU on t_gpu_pool_3. Requests with long seq_len hitting continuous-batch path and triggering shared-kv-storm.

liam: thanks. quick check: any recent rollout of batching flags? I saw devex changed default batch_window to 20ms yesterday for new models.

ashok: that was a rollout but gated by feature flag `continuous_batch_v2` and should be canaryed. Checking rollout status now.

nina: customers reporting timeouts to embeddings endpoint. alert correlates with increased tail latency from ~120ms -> 1.8s on policy-service route.

devex: confirmed, `continuous_batch_v2` was turned on for 40% of traffic across the cohort yesterday at 03:10 UTC. Canary config shows 40% global, excluded for enterprise tier, but per-customer override can exist.

maria: step 1: reduce surface area. Let's set canary to 5% globally and apply per-customer override to disable for impacted accounts. Who has the oncall right to flip the flag? @liam you have perms, yes?

liam: I can do the flag flip. I'll change the canary to 5% and set per-cust overrides for the top 3 impacted tenants (cust-A, cust-B, cust-C). Doing it now.

liam: executing:
```
# change canary
./flagctl set continuous_batch_v2 --percent 5 --scope global --who liam
# disable for customers
./flagctl set continuous_batch_v2 --value off --customer cust-A,cust-B,cust-C --who liam
``` 

ops-bot: FLAG CHANGE: `continuous_batch_v2` set to 5% global by liam at 2026-03-15T15:12:37Z. Per-customer disable applied for cust-A,cust-B,cust-C. Audit-id: a1b2c3

maria: watch metrics for next 5 minutes. I'm starting an emergency canary (lightweight) that routes a small set of synthetic traffic to validate cache behavior.

ashok: looking at KV metrics: total_kv_evictions drops immediately after flag change. p95 latency trending down from 1.8s -> 280ms within 90s. good sign.

nina: customer support: cust-A confirmed reduced errors. They're still seeing occasional retries but overall back to normal. I'll message CSM.

sre-rotation: log snippet from problematic worker:
```
W kv_cache.cpp:982 evicting 1200 entries in 2ms (cache_pressure=0.92)
E batch_scheduler.cpp:432 drop request due to cache-miss storm
``` 

devex: quick note: we also have a per-region override for ap-southeast where the rollout was 60% because of traffic shaping. I just reverted that too (set to 0 for ap-southeast).

liam: did that revert. ops-bot: confirm.

ops-bot: FLAG CHANGE: `continuous_batch_v2` set to 0% for region ap-southeast by liam. Audit-id: d4e5f6

maria: ok mitigation working. next step: prepare hotfix to batch config to avoid kv blowups when ephemeral cache pressure spikes. Will open PR with safe defaults: cap per-request merged-batch-size, enable KV-proactive-eviction-threshold, and reduce batch_window for long-seq requests.

ashok: add a circuit-breaker so if kv_evictions/sec > 100 then fall back to legacy batching for that host. We should be able to flip on/off with feature flag per-customer.

devex: suggested canary rollout plan in thread: start 1% global on non-enterprise, shadow 2% for 30m, then ramp 5/20/50. Per-customer opt-in for critical tenants only after manual approval.

maria: agreed. Also notify product and support. nina please draft a short blurb for support to send to affected customers: timeline, current status, mitigation, and ETA for permanent fix.

nina: on it. draft:
"We're investigating intermittent latency and errors for text-generation endpoints due to a batching-related cache regression. We've reduced the canary and applied per-customer overrides; impacted traffic is stable. Engineering is working on a hotfix; we'll update in 2 hours or sooner."

liam: starting canary for hotfix build-2026.03.15-hotfix-1 to 1% traffic on a single canary pool. Command:
```
./deployctl rollout --image build-2026.03.15-hotfix-1 --pool canary-1 --percent 1
``` 

ops-bot: DEPLOY START: rollout build-2026.03.15-hotfix-1 -> canary-1 (1%) by liam. Track: https://go/internal/deploys/1791234567

ashok: monitoring canary logs and KV metrics. will report back in 10m.

(10m passes)

ashok: canary metrics look good. no evictions spike, latency stable. I'll approve a gradual bump to 10% and include a per-customer kill switch in the rollout.

liam: bumping to 10%.

ops-bot: DEPLOY UPDATE: canary-1 bumped to 10% by liam.

maria: nice. I'm going to codify per-customer override tooling in the runbook so support can disable for a tenant without eng intervention. Add CLI snippet and UI path.

devex: PR opened: https://go/internal/pulls/5123 - includes circuit-breaker, cap, and flag controls. Requesting review from ashok and maria.

ashok: quick review done, left minor comment on metric naming. once merged we'll schedule a canary ramp to 50% then full.

nina: customers updated. cust-A and cust-B acknowledged and are monitoring.

maria: resolution summary: immediate mitigation was to reduce `continuous_batch_v2` global canary to 5% and apply per-customer disables; reverted region-specific rollout; deployed hotfix build-2026.03.15-hotfix-1 via canary with per-customer kill switches; observed p95 drop to baseline and eviction rate normalized. No data leakage or SLO breaches recorded.

maria: next actions (owner):
- ashok: merge hotfix PR and run full rollout (owner)
- devex: add runbook snippets and flag UI docs (owner)
- nina: follow-up comms to customers + post-incident note (owner)
- liam: create postmortem and include why region rollout diverged from global policy (owner)

liam: will draft postmortem today and assign.

maria: closing page. If anything flares up, re-open thread. thx team :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED -> 1791234567. Duration: 12m. Links: https://go/internal/incidents/1791234567
